findings.failure_path: Following the required boundary walk on an authentication, payment, or customer-data flow logs entry/exit data and the actual env/config at every component. Those logs may already be persisted or exported before Phase B copy-time sanitization, so later ticket redaction cannot undo disclosure of secrets, PII, payloads, or internal endpoints.
findings.smallest_fix: Require allowlisted, redacted boundary metadata at instrumentation time; explicitly prohibit raw bodies, headers, secrets, PII, and env/config values, with ephemeral local inspection as the fallback.

findings.failure_path: The unconditional instruction to use a pathspec excludes commits outside the initially suspected paths. A dependency manifest, shared library, generator, build configuration, or schema change can cause the failure while touching none of those paths, so bisect can omit the real culprit and return a false boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Make path restriction conditional on evidence that the cause is confined to those paths, and require retrying the full commit range when the restricted search does not produce a valid causal boundary.

findings.failure_path: A multi-component production incident may be historical, non-retriggerable, partially observable, or unsafe to instrument across every component. Requiring one new instrumented run before hypotheses can be formed blocks the telemetry-driven route added earlier in the same diff.
findings.smallest_fix: Condition the single-run boundary walk on a safely reproducible and fully accessible chain; otherwise route to existing telemetry, partial boundary evidence, or layer narrowing and record the visibility gap.

findings.failure_path: The table defines a falsifier as an observation only the hypothesis predicts. That is confirming or discriminating evidence, not an observation incompatible with the hypothesis, so agents can record the wrong test and incorrectly promote an unfalsified cause.
findings.smallest_fix: Change the column to an observation that cannot occur if the hypothesis is true, and add a separate predicted-observation column if positive discriminating evidence is needed.

findings.failure_path: The only landed evidence records the base SHA. Because the profile's self-review and evidence entries are claims rather than proof, the packet cannot establish primary-page attribution, the 5000-word and 500-line limits, immutable-anchor preservation, exact source-register anchoring, or clean checker results; a release could therefore pass solely on unverified assertions.
findings.smallest_fix: Add bounded reproducible evidence containing the relevant command outputs and primary-source URL/date excerpts, re-freeze the candidate, and review that evidence with the diff.

concern_results.conclusion: Not satisfied: path-restricted bisection is made unconditional, and the playbook mislabels a uniquely predicted observation as a falsifier.
Not satisfied: the mandatory boundary walk instructs agents to log boundary data and actual env/config without probe-time redaction, creating a credential and PII exposure path.
Not satisfied: the mandatory single-run localization has no fallback for historical incidents, inaccessible components, or failures that cannot safely be retriggered.
Not satisfied: the diff supplies only a base-SHA attestation; claimed size, checker, anchor, attribution, and semantic-control results cannot be independently verified from the bounded packet.
Frontmatter is unchanged, but the unconditional pathspec and single-run requirements can regress previously valid diagnosis workflows.
The documentation-only change appears reversible and introduces no migration or irreversible state transition; release readiness remains blocked by the evidence gap.
The telemetry routes are operationally useful, but logging raw boundary values and configuration conflicts with safe observability and incident-handling practice.
